spec_coverage.note: Specifications/dev-workflow-platform.md (74 FRs) targets the portal/ app, not Source/. Zero of those FRs are referenced in Source/ — this is expected given the two-app architecture, not an implementation gap.

findings.title: GET /api/search NOT wired into app.ts
findings.detail: FR-dependency-search requires a GET /api/search endpoint for cross-entity typeahead. The route was implemented in portal/ but never wired into Source/Backend/src/app.ts. The test file search.test.ts explicitly documents: 'As of this review cycle the GET /api/search endpoint is NOT wired into Source/Backend/src/app.ts. These tests document the expected contract and will FAIL until the route is implemented.' No search.ts or equivalent route file exists in Source/Backend/src/routes/.
findings.recommendation: Implement GET /api/search?q= in Source/Backend/src/routes/ that searches work item title/description, and register it in app.ts as app.use('/api/search', searchRouter).
findings.cross_ref: Source/Backend/tests/routes/search.test.ts — tests are already written and waiting

findings.title: Logger never pretty-prints in development — violates CLAUDE.md architecture rule
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md requires 'structured JSON logging in production, pretty-printing in development'. The logger implementation always calls process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(entry)) regardless of NODE_ENV. There is no environment check anywhere in logger.ts or its shim (src/logger.ts). In development, log output is machine-readable JSON, making local debugging harder than necessary.
findings.recommendation: Add NODE_ENV check: when NODE_ENV !== 'production', emit human-readable format (e.g. `[LEVEL] message {context}`). Only emit raw JSON in production.

findings.title: 7 of 8 plan requirements files fail traceability enforcer
findings.detail: The traceability enforcer auto-selects the most-recently-modified requirements.md (currently Plans/self-judging-workflow/requirements.md). Running it against all plans reveals 7 failures: image-upload (FR-083–FR-089, FR-XXX), duplicate-deprecated-status (FR-DUP-06–FR-DUP-13), dependency-linking (FR-0002–FR-0007, FR-070, FR-085), dev-cycle-traceability (FR-063–FR-069, FR-XXX), orchestrated-dev-cycles (FR-043–FR-049, FR-XXX), orchestrator-cycle-dashboard (FR-070–FR-076, FR-0XX), dev-workflow-platform (FR-027–FR-032, FR-XXX, FR-XXXX). Most of these target the portal/ app, not Source/, but the enforcer has no awareness of that split.
findings.recommendation: Add a --scope flag or config to the enforcer to map plan requirements to their target source directory (portal/ vs Source/). Or create a CI step that runs the enforcer against each plan with the correct --source-dirs argument. Short-term: document which plans target portal/ vs Source/ so the CI gate reflects reality.

findings.title: Duplicate test suites for WorkItemDetailPage and WorkItemListPage
findings.detail: Two separate test files exist for the same components: tests/WorkItemDetailPage.test.tsx (368 lines) and tests/pages/WorkItemDetailPage.test.tsx (393 lines); similarly tests/WorkItemListPage.test.tsx (286 lines) and tests/pages/WorkItemListPage.test.tsx (262 lines). Both target the same production components but have slightly different coverage. It is unclear which is authoritative. Duplicate suites risk divergence: one may catch regressions the other misses, and both consume CI time.
findings.recommendation: Audit both test files for each component, consolidate into the tests/pages/ location (matching the production src/pages/ structure), and delete the top-level duplicates. Ensure 100% traceability comment coverage is preserved in the surviving file.

findings.title: Two logger modules — shim anti-pattern increases maintenance surface
findings.detail: There are two logger files: src/utils/logger.ts (canonical) and src/logger.ts (shim/adapter). The shim was added to bridge different call signatures between coders. This means two import paths exist in production code: workItemStore.ts uses '../utils/logger' while all routes use '../logger' (shim). A change to the canonical logger API requires updating the shim. The comment 'Backend-coder-2's workflow routes import logger as default from this module' reveals this is a workaround for inter-agent coordination, not an architectural decision.
findings.recommendation: Unify on a single logger interface. Either update all call sites to use utils/logger directly with a named export, or absorb the normalization logic into utils/logger itself and delete the shim.

findings.title: Specifications/dev-workflow-platform.md covers portal/ app — zero Source/ references
findings.detail: The main Specifications/ directory contains dev-workflow-platform.md (74 FRs for a SQLite + feature-requests + dev-cycles product) and workflow-engine.md (the actual spec for Source/). The dev-workflow-platform.md FRs (FR-001–FR-069) map entirely to portal/ not Source/. Running the traceability enforcer with Specifications/ as the target against Source/ would show 0% coverage — misleading to any automation or reviewer that scans specs/ without understanding the two-app architecture.
findings.recommendation: Add a header comment to Specifications/dev-workflow-platform.md: 'This specification governs portal/ (the SQLite-backed dev workflow platform). Source/ is governed by workflow-engine.md.' Also update inspector.config.yml to document the two-product boundary.

findings.title: getAllItems() called unbounded in dashboard service (3x)
findings.detail: dashboardService.ts calls getAllItems() three separate times (lines 14, 33, 58) to compute summary, activity, and queue data. getAllItems() returns the full in-memory store with no pagination or limit. With a large number of work items, all three calls iterate the entire store independently. The inspector.config.yml static_checks list explicitly calls out 'Unbounded Map iteration (no slice/limit on work item list)' as a concern.
findings.recommendation: Call getAllItems() once per request and reuse the result across all three computations. For long-term scalability, consider adding a maxActivity parameter to the activity computation to cap the returned items (e.g., last 50 events only).

findings.title: eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps in 2 production files — undocumented suppression
findings.detail: Two production frontend files suppress the react-hooks/exhaustive-deps rule without explaining WHY the dependency is intentionally excluded: useWorkItems.ts:63 and DependencyPicker.tsx:82. CLAUDE.md architecture rules prohibit silently suppressing linting. The hook dependency arrays are manually curated (specific filter fields listed) which suggests intentional stable references, but this is not documented.
findings.recommendation: Add an inline comment above each eslint-disable explaining the suppression reason (e.g., '// refreshKey is the only trigger we want; listing individual filter fields prevents re-runs on unrelated parent re-renders'). Or refactor to use useCallback/useMemo to satisfy the linter properly.

findings.title: FR-dependency-seed never implemented — no seed.ts in Source/Backend
findings.detail: Plans/dependency-linking/requirements.md Implementation Delta explicitly marks FR-dependency-seed as missing: 'No seed.ts file exists in portal/Backend/src/database/'. For the Source/ in-memory implementation this means there is no idempotent seeding of known dependency relationships (e.g., the 5 BUG-0010 blockers). Manual testing cannot reproduce the documented dependency scenarios without hand-crafting API calls.
findings.recommendation: Implement a seed function in Source/Backend/src/store/workItemStore.ts or a new Source/Backend/src/utils/seed.ts that creates known items and their dependency links on startup in development/test mode. Call it from app.ts when NODE_ENV === 'development'.

findings.title: Traceability enforcer checks only the most-recently-modified plan — CI gate is incomplete
findings.detail: The enforcer's default mode selects the most-recently-modified requirements.md via os.path.getmtime. The CLAUDE.md verification gate (`python3 tools/traceability-enforcer.py`) therefore only validates one plan at a time, providing a false sense of overall traceability. 7 plans currently fail when checked individually.
findings.recommendation: Add a --all flag to the enforcer that iterates every requirements.md under Plans/, runs traceability for each, and fails CI if any has untraced FRs. Or create a wrapper script tools/check-all-traceability.sh and add it to the CLAUDE.md verification gates section.
findings.cross_ref: CLAUDE.md Testing Rules verification gates, tools/traceability-enforcer.py:45
